course_name_original: Fatiga, Corrosión Bajo Tensión y Fluencia
course_name_en: Fatigue, Stress Corrosion Cracking and Creep
prerequisites: A general materials science course in a previous Bachelor's degree
First-semester courses of the Interuniversity Master's in Integrity and Durability of Materials, Components and Structures

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to evaluate the resistance of materials against corrosive actions at low and high temperatures and to make decisions for their protection against these types of actions.

Ability to handle and use different testing techniques employed in the microstructural and mechanical characterization of materials, evaluate oxidation/corrosion resistance, perform corresponding measurements, and interpret the results obtained in all these tests.
Ability to apply theoretical models and use physical and mathematical tools for diagnosing and solving problems.
Ability to evaluate the structural integrity of components subjected to mechanical loads and predict their useful life in situations of fatigue, stress corrosion cracking, and creep.
Know the methods and numerical models for analyzing materials, components, and structures.
Knowledge of aging mechanisms, including the consequences of damage mechanisms on the macroscopic behavior of materials and structures.
Know the tools available for the practical execution of failure analysis.
Know a wide variety of practical cases in which the causes of failure of real structural components are determined.
Acquisition of laboratory skills and systematic work to mechanically characterize different materials and evaluate their durability.
Handle the scientific equipment used in these subjects to design specific tests or experiments and to interpret the results obtained from them.
Calculate critical loads and critical defect sizes of cracked components subjected to any type of loads.
Know and apply predictive models capable of extrapolating the behavior of systems, structures, and components for a defined period of use.
Write a scientific paper concisely and present it orally with clarity.
Promote in the student a desire for the acquisition of practical knowledge.
Advance the student's ability to apply acquired engineering knowledge.
Foster an open, critical, cooperative, and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: Cyclic deformation. Stress approach. Strain approach
Allowable defects and fatigue life. Design
Mechanisms of fatigue crack propagation. Metallurgical variables
Cases: crack propagation in different materials: ceramics, plastics, composites
The phenomenon of SCC. Embrittlement models
SCC in metals and alloys. Calculation of propagation and life in components
teaching_methods: External internships (in other institutions or companies)

assessment_methods.method: Tests at the end of each block
Written test on full course content (theoretical part, including lab practices)
Written test on full course content (practical part)

assessment_rules: Tests at the end of each block and completed laboratory practice scripts account for 40% of the final grade (30% for tests, 10% for practice scripts). A final evaluation session, consisting of a written test on the complete course content, makes up the remaining 60%. This final test has a theoretical part (20% of the final grade, including laboratory practices) and a practical part (40% of the final grade). A minimum of 4 points out of 10 in this final evaluation is required to pass the subject.
